sections.finding: Lines 81-83 route capability resolution through runner.executors.<id>.for[] but resolveExecutorAndOverrides (resolve.mjs:255-266) states an executor's own for never binds a purpose and only capabilities.<name>.prefer does; for[] is read only by resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints (resolve.mjs:53) to infer a capability label; the same defect also sits in the code block at lines 81-83. The rest (purpose terminology, resolveExecutorIdForPurpose not exported, selector.type purpose at plan.mjs:91) is true.

Item 2 (line 270-271) says resolveExecutorAndOverrides resolves capability aliases and executor for[] declarations, but that function binds only executor-id, default executor and capabilities.<name>.prefer (resolve.mjs:269-310); alias handling and for[] live in resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints (resolve.mjs:25-66). Forbidden-dependency list is true (test import-graph forbids appendEvent/settleClaim/pickWork/returnWork in src/runner/dispatch; cohort-planner has no source hits).

line 63 says structured claims carrying another Run identity are rejected, but run-result.mjs:155 and 297 reject a RunResult record whose runId differs from expectedRunId; the worker claim validator has no runId check at all

Line 72 states as a ported invariant that blocked means do not retry, but herdr-round.mjs:344-357 maps blocked to worker-timeout and RECOVERY in recovery.mjs retries that class (the code comment calls it a known seam), so current callers do retry blocked rounds. The ladder order, death threshold 3, 15s credential probe (liveness.mjs:267-299) and provider-limit emission are otherwise correct; qualify line 72 as the ladder verdict only.

Lines 94-97 state cancellation-bars-retry and budget-exhaustion precedence as behavior, yet cancel is explicitly parked as cancel-unsupported (herdr-reconcile.mjs:344, reconcile-cli-spawn.mjs:40, detached-run-supervisor.mjs:981-985) and recovery.mjs/recovery-planner.mjs have no budget or cancellation path; the status row calls this section current standalone Run recovery.

Lines 156-165: result.json is published via publishImmutableProof (settlement.mjs:434), not publishMutableProjection, and the sentence that unsupported filesystem guarantees refuse mutation with a named diagnostic has no code (run-lock.mjs publish only rethrows non-EEXIST link errors) nor any doctor probe (no match in src/setup). H1 holder identity (buildRunControlHolder run-lock.mjs:51, resolveHolderLiveness decision table in process-identity.mjs:70-90) is described correctly.

S2 row (line 225) is marked Implemented adapter scope while its scope lists handle guard, pending-control reconciliation and material capture; git grep finds zero hits for RunHandle or RecoveryMaterial and no pending-control code, only herdr launch reconciliation (herdr-reconcile.mjs) exists. S0/S1/S3/S4/S5 rows are consistent (run-lock.mjs, recovery.mjs, recover.mjs, commit 2180b4e72 exists).

mostly true (agent-result-claim v2 at agent-result-claim-contract.mjs:5, legacy-derived and contract-corrupt provenance, reconciliation negations match fgos dispatch --help, test and archive record exist) BUT line 263 says new results are v2 while normalizeRunResult defaults contractVersion to 3 and v4 is also written (run-result.mjs:13-16,350,562)
item 4 lists role and budget as optional inline fields, but execution-contract.mjs:345 requires a non-empty contract.role and lines 371-380 require contract.budget with positive timeoutMs and maxRuns

Lines 197-198 say both decide --for and execute --for use capability-aware resolution, but cli.mjs:1081-1093 refuses execute --for outright (message: execute --for is no longer supported); lines 199-200 say the primary Rust-host request door uses bind(), yet bind() is only called from execution/run.mjs:404, assignment-runner.mjs and setup, with no Rust caller. Selector list itself (plan.mjs:80-93) is correct.

Example at lines 300 and 302 uses minTier, a retired field that assignment-policy.mjs now rejects with a removed error and registrations.mjs:657-658 reports as a dead key (rigor replaced it); table row 289 says constraints are unioned but assignment-policy.mjs:459-462 spreads opPolicy.constraints over the base (override); row 291 says broader fallbacks are appended but assignment-policy.mjs:380-388 keeps only the most specific fallbackExecutors and marks them reserved-not-executed.
